\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\scriptsize\vspace{0.5ex}
\textit{Notes:} Joint test of Simonsohn, Simmons and Nelson (2020). For every specification $k$ the outcome is replaced by $y^*_k = y - \hat\beta_k x_k$, where $x_k$ is the term of interest ($x=\mathrm{POP}$, or $\mathrm{POP}\times\mathrm{IDEO}$ for the interaction), so that the null of a zero coefficient holds exactly in every specification. In each of $B=500$ draws, parties (CMP party codes) are resampled with replacement, the same draw is used for all specifications, and every specification is re-estimated on its null outcome; $p<0.05$ uses standard errors clustered by party (each resampled copy a separate cluster). $p$ is the share of draws with a median at least as negative, or a share at least as large, as observed; $<0.002$ means that no draw was as extreme. Shares are over the specifications estimable in a draw.
\end{minipage}
